connections.observation: s001 marks λοιπά opening with two virtues and λοιπόν closing with one remaining; s013 frames the section with δικαιοσύνη named as ultimate aim at opening and as the remaining εἶδος at close; s014 pairs κατιδεῖν (the seeing-task proposed) with κατῶπται (the seeing-task completed for three). Held together, these three configurations make visible the section's enacted completion of one examination (σωφροσύνη) positioned between two framings of what remains (δικαιοσύνη).

s002 concentrates κρείττων densely across the section; s003 sets κρείττων and ἥττων in explicit paradoxical opposition (the one stronger than himself is also weaker); s007 clusters the κρατ- family in active and passive forms. Together these make visible the section's absorption in forms of mastery that circle a paradox: the same person both masters and is mastered by himself, articulated through overlapping lexical registers.

s004 traces the better/worse pair moving from the soul of a single human to the city's natural consonance; s008 traces ἄρχω moving from the better part ruling the worse within to rulers and ruled sharing δόξα about who should rule. Held together, these parallel migrations make visible the section's transfer of an internal relation (better ruling worse in one soul) into a civic relation (rulers and ruled in one city), with both migrations converging in the final definition of σωφροσύνη at 432a.

s005 accumulates musical/harmonic vocabulary (συμφωνία, ἁρμονία, συνᾴδω, ὁμόνοια); s010 presents τέταται as a spatial-musical image of σωφροσύνη stretched through the whole; s011 names weakest, strongest, and middle singing in unison, using musical string terminology. Together these make visible the section's sustained musical figuration, where temperance is not a property located in one part but a harmonic stretching (τέταται) that makes diverse registers (weakest/strongest/middle) sound together (συνᾴδοντας).

s009 contrasts ἐν μέρει (courage and wisdom each in a part) with διʼ ὅλης … διὰ πασῶν (temperance through the whole); s016 records the question whether temperance belongs to rulers or ruled and the answer ἐν ἀμφοτέροις, refusing the disjunction. Held together, these make visible the section's insistence that σωφροσύνη differs structurally from other virtues by refusing localization—it cannot be assigned to one part, class, or role.

s006 tracks ἐπιθυμία shifting from individual self-mastery to the city's desires being mastered by the few; s007 clusters κρατ- vocabulary in active and passive forms; s002 concentrates κρείττων densely, first in the self-mastery paradox, then transferred to the city. Together these make visible the section's movement from the puzzle of one person mastering his own desires to the city's structure in which the desires of many are mastered by the desires (and φρόνησις) of few, re-enacting at civic scale the internal configuration named κρείττω αὑτοῦ.

s004 traces the better/worse pair; s015 pairs βέλτιστα with two participles—φῦσιν and παιδευθεῖσιν—linking nature and education. Held together, these make visible that those who possess simple, measured desires guided by νοῦς and ὀρθὴ δόξα are described as best both by nature and by education, suggesting that the better part's rule depends on both φύσις and παιδεία, a doubling that recurs in the final definition (432a: κατὰ φύσιν συμφωνίαν).

s012 calls the common phrase κρείττω αὑτοῦ an ἴχνος (trace/track) of σωφροσύνη; s005 accumulates musical/harmonic vocabulary culminating in ὁμόνοια. Held together, these make visible the section's method: it begins by tracking a proverbial trace (ἴχνη αὐτῆς λέγεται), follows that trace through the paradox of self-mastery, and arrives at a musical-harmonic definition (ὁμόνοια, συμφωνία) that the trace pointed toward but did not name.

s008 traces ἄρχω from the better ruling the worse to rulers and ruled sharing δόξα about who should rule; s016 answers the question of where σωφρονεῖν resides with ἐν ἀμφοτέροις, refusing to assign it to either rulers or ruled alone. Together these make visible that σωφροσύνη is defined not by who rules but by shared δόξα about ruling—the same belief (ἡ αὐτὴ δόξα) held by both ἄρχοντες and ἀρχόμενοι concerning who should rule.

s010 presents τέταται, the perfect passive of τείνω, as the verb describing how σωφροσύνη is stretched through the whole city; s009 contrasts this διʼ ὅλης … διὰ πασῶν extension with the ἐν μέρει location of courage and wisdom. Held together, these make visible the unique spatial grammar of temperance: where other virtues reside (ἐνοῦσα ἐν μέρει), temperance is tensed or stretched (τέταται), a perfect passive suggesting both completed action and sustained tension across the civic body.

elements.context: αἳ δὴ μετὰ νοῦ τε καὶ δόξης ὀρθῆς λογισμῷ ἄγονται
ἡ αὐτὴ δόξα ἔνεστι τοῖς τε ἄρχουσι καὶ ἀρχομένοις

new_signals.observation: δόξα appears first as ὀρθὴ δόξα guiding the few with νοῦς, then as ἡ αὐτὴ δόξα shared by rulers and ruled about who should rule—a shift from correct belief as internal guide to same belief as civic agreement.

elements.context: τάς γε πολλὰς καὶ παντοδαπὰς ἐπιθυμίας
ἐν τοῖς πολλοῖς τε καὶ φαύλοις
τὰς ἐν τοῖς πολλοῖς τε καὶ φαύλοις

new_signals.observation: πολύς recurs, naming first the many and varied desires, then the many and base people in whom such desires are found—a lexical echo linking numerical plurality with ethical inferiority.

elements.context: τῆς φρονήσεως τῆς ἐν τοῖς ἐλάττοσί τε καὶ ἐπιεικεστέροις

new_signals.observation: ὀλίγοις and ἐλάττοσί both name the few, paired first with simple desires guided by νοῦς, then with φρόνησις that masters the desires of the many—a consistent minority identified by both number and ethical quality.

elements.context: ἐν παισὶ μάλιστα ἄν τις εὕροι

new_signals.observation: Children, women, and household slaves are grouped in a parallel series as the primary locus of many and varied desires and pleasures—a civic-domestic grouping of those assumed to lack self-governance.

elements.context: διʼ ὅλης ἀτεχνῶς τέταται διὰ πασῶν

new_signals.observation: διὰ πασῶν is the Greek musical term for 'through all [notes],' naming the octave—a technical musical reference making the harmonic metaphor explicit and precise.
